stem: What does quality mean in business?

options.content: Meeting customers' expectations and being fit for purpose
Always using the most expensive materials available
options.rationale: Quality does not require expensive materials.

options.content: Producing as many units as possible every day
Selling at the highest possible price

explanation: A product is good quality if it meets customers' expectations for the price they pay.

options.content: Inspecting products to find and remove faulty items
options.rationale: Correct: usually at the end of production.

options.content: Making every worker responsible for quality at every stage
Small groups of workers discussing quality problems
Agreeing standards with suppliers before production
options.rationale: That is part of quality assurance.

explanation: **Quality control** finds faults by inspection; it does not prevent them.

stem: What is the main difference between quality assurance and quality control?

options.content: Assurance is only used by small businesses
options.rationale: Both are used by businesses of all sizes.

options.content: Control involves all of the workers; assurance uses only specialist inspectors
options.rationale: It is the other way round.

options.content: Assurance prevents faults at each stage; control finds them after production
Assurance checks only finished products

explanation: Control **finds** faults; assurance **prevents** them by checking at every stage.

stem: Eight machinists at a clothing factory meet every Friday to discuss why seams are splitting and suggest improvements. What is this?

options.content: Quality control by inspectors
A quality circle
options.rationale: Correct: workers meet to solve quality problems.

options.content: A focus group of customers
Test marketing of a new product
options.rationale: No product is being tested in a market.

explanation: A **quality circle** is a small group of workers who identify and solve quality problems.

stem: Which is a disadvantage of quality control?

options.content: Faulty goods are found and removed before reaching customers
Faults are found after materials and time have been wasted
It is easy for workers to understand
It needs little training for production workers

explanation: Control finds faults late and does not tackle their causes; inspectors are an extra cost.

stem: Why might total quality management improve worker motivation?

options.content: Workers no longer have to check their own work
options.rationale: In TQM workers do check their work.

options.content: Wages are always increased under TQM
options.rationale: TQM does not require pay rises.

options.content: Workers are given responsibility and their ideas are valued
Managers make all decisions without consulting staff

explanation: TQM and quality circles give workers responsibility and recognition, which can motivate them.

stem: For which business would quality assurance at every stage be most important?

options.content: A stall selling second-hand books
options.rationale: Faults are easy to see and low risk.

options.content: A firm printing party invitations
options.rationale: Faults are low risk and easy to check at the end.

options.content: A shop selling plastic buckets
A factory making medicines
options.rationale: Correct: a single fault could harm patients.

explanation: When faults are dangerous, they must be prevented at every stage, not just found at the end.
hints: Where would a fault be most dangerous?

stem: Which is a cost of poor quality to a business?

options.content: More repeat customers
A better reputation
The ability to charge higher prices
Refunds, replacements and lost customers

explanation: Poor quality brings waste, refunds, complaints, lost customers and damage to reputation.

stem: In total quality management every employee is responsible for quality.
explanation: True. TQM involves everyone in every department.

stem: A low-priced product can never be of good quality.
explanation: False. Quality means meeting expectations for the price; a cheap product can be good quality.

stem: Match each term with its description.

right.content: Every employee responsible for quality, aiming at zero defects
Workers meeting to solve quality problems
Checking at every stage to prevent faults

explanation: Control finds; assurance prevents; TQM involves everyone; circles involve workers in solutions.

payload.template: The aim of total quality management is {{blank:a}} defects. In TQM the next department in a process is treated as an {{blank:b}} customer.

explanation: TQM aims at zero defects and treats colleagues as internal customers.

stem: A factory made 2,500 jars of jam and rejected 60. Calculate the reject rate as a percentage, to one decimal place.
Each rejected jar in the previous question cost US\$3.50 to make. Calculate the cost of the 60 rejected jars.
Explain **two** reasons why quality is important to a business.

points.description: Reason 1, e.g. customer loyalty / repeat sales.
Explained: satisfied customers return and recommend the business.
Reason 2, e.g. lower costs of waste and returns / higher price / reputation.
Explained: fewer refunds and scrapped goods / premium price / easier to win retailers.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Good quality keeps customers satisfied, so they return and recommend the business to others, raising sales. It also reduces waste, refunds and replacements, which lowers costs.

explanation: Quality affects sales, reputation, price and costs.

stem:
Farai's factory in Bulawayo makes plastic water tanks. At present, two inspectors check every tank at the end of production. Customers have complained about leaking tanks. Production data are shown below.

| Month | Units produced | Units rejected |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| January | 4,000 | 180 |
| February | 4,200 | 168 |
| March | 4,100 | 205 |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the reject rate in March as a percentage.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Each rejected tank costs US\$20 in materials, but US\$2 of plastic can be recycled from it, so the net cost is US\$18 a tank. Calculate the total net cost of the tanks rejected over the three months.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain why quality control has not stopped customers complaining.

points.description: Inspectors find faults only after the tanks are made.
Some faults are missed (leaks may not show in inspection).
It does not tackle the cause of the faults, so reject rates stay high.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Recommend whether Farai should introduce quality assurance with quality circles. Justify your answer.

points.description: Uses data: reject rate 4-5% and rising in March; rejects cost US\$9,954 in three months.
QA prevents faults at each stage (moulding, fitting, sealing) so fewer rejects and leaks.
Quality circles use machinists' knowledge to find causes; may motivate.
Costs: training, time for meetings, slower at first; workers' commitment needed.
Could keep a final leak test while QA is introduced.
Justified recommendation.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Rejects cost about US\$9,954 in three months and the March reject rate rose to 5%, while leaking tanks still reach customers. Quality assurance would make workers check each stage, such as moulding and sealing, preventing faults instead of finding them late, and quality circles would use the machinists' knowledge to find why tanks leak. Training and meetings cost money and time, and success depends on workers' commitment. Because the waste and complaints are costly and rising, Farai should introduce quality assurance with quality circles, keeping a final leak test until the reject rate falls.

explanation: (a) 5%. (b) US\$9,954. (c) Control finds faults late and misses causes. (d) QA with quality circles, justified with the data.
hints: (b) Add the three months' rejects first.

stem: Chipo runs a small catering enterprise in Gweru that supplies school canteens. She has six workers. Two schools have complained about cold food and late deliveries. Chipo is considering introducing total quality management.

points.description: Every employee is responsible for quality at all times.
Aim of zero defects / complete customer satisfaction / continuous improvement.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Explain how TQM could solve **two** of Chipo's problems.

points.description: Cold food: cooks and drivers check temperatures / use insulated containers at each stage.
Because everyone sees the school as the customer.
Late deliveries: drivers and kitchen plan times together / internal customer idea (kitchen supplies drivers on time).
Problems found and fixed by workers themselves.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Evaluate whether TQM is suitable for Chipo's enterprise.

points.description: Small team: easy to involve all six workers.
Service quality depends on every worker (cooks, drivers).
Cost of training and time; Chipo's limited budget.
Benefits take time; schools may cancel contracts first.
Quick fixes also needed (insulated boxes, earlier departure).
Justified conclusion.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: With only six workers, Chipo can easily involve everyone, and in catering quality depends on every person, from the cook to the driver. TQM would make each worker responsible for food being hot and on time. However, training takes time and money, and benefits may come slowly while the schools want immediate improvement. Chipo should make quick changes now, such as insulated containers and earlier departures, and introduce simple TQM practices such as weekly team meetings to review complaints. A small, low-cost version of TQM suits her enterprise.

explanation: TQM suits small service teams if kept simple and combined with quick practical fixes.
hints: (b) Link each problem to workers checking their own stage.
(c) Weigh the small team against cost and time.
